subject: Post-demo: prompt traceability & retention — follow up and options
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T16:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: prompt traceability & retention — follow up and options

Hi Sarah — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and follow-ups from the demo with your engineering and compliance teams: what we heard is that ClearHealth needs: 1) clarity on exactly what is stored for prompts and model outputs; 2) an option to prevent storage of PII-containing prompts/outputs; and 3) confirmation of data residency and auditability for token-level logs.

High-level from our side: Redwood’s hosted API has a default telemetry & retention posture we can tailor for pilots — details below. I attached a short PDF with the traceability model and retention controls (redwood-prompt-traceability.pdf) and our data-retention overview. Please review and tell us which of the following you want us to configure for the pilot: 

- Option A: No persistent prompt/output storage (ephemeral logs only for 72h for troubleshooting, then auto-deleted)
- Option B: Prompt input stored for 30 days, outputs only stored if explicitly flagged for evaluation; PII redaction enabled
- Option C: Dedicated deployment with customer-managed logs and configurable retention (can be zero days)

Questions for you: Do you need token-level transcripts for debugging (these include de-tokenized text) or will hashed digests be sufficient for traceability? Also, do you require EU-only residency for any test/prod workloads?

Next steps: please share your compliance contact (I think Tom Baxter is on the thread?) and we’ll propose a mutual action plan for a pilot config.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-data-retention-overview.pdf]
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@clearhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@clearhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T20:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt traceability & retention — follow up and options

Thanks Hannah — useful recap. A few clarifications from our security/compliance side: 

- Primary ask: Do you persist raw prompt inputs or raw model outputs by default, and for how long? We need a definitive answer we can include in our vendor memo.
- PII requirement: we cannot allow storage of unredacted direct identifiers (SSN, MRN, full name + DOB together) without explicit contractual terms. Is there a built-in redaction pipeline?
- Auditability: we need an immutable audit trail that proves when data was ingested and when it was purged. Does Redwood provide tamper-evident logs or an exportable audit file?
- Token logs: we are open to hashed token transcripts for debugging, but need to know: what hashing algorithm, where are salts stored, and can we use our own salt/KMS?

Tom is our compliance lead (cc'd). If possible, can you provide a two-paragraph summary we can share with procurement and our security review team that answers the first two bullets? Also — are SOC 2 and ISO docs available for review?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Head of Product Security, ClearHealth Solutions
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt traceability & retention — follow up and options

Sarah — great questions. Below is a concise, shareable answer you can forward to procurement/security; I’ve also included implementation notes for your engineers.

Short answer for procurement/security (2 paragraphs):
Redwood does not persist customer data beyond configured retention windows unless you opt into persistent logging for evaluation. On hosted plans our default is ephemeral retention for prompts/outputs (72 hours) used only for debugging and quality-monitoring; those logs are automatically purged. For Dedicated or Private deployments, customers can select longer or zero-day retention windows and control where logs are stored (US/EU).
We provide redaction hooks and a client-side hashing option so you can remove or hash direct identifiers before they reach our servers. For auditability we export ingestion/retention events in a machine-readable audit file (JSON/CSV) on request; SOC 2 and ISO artifacts are available under NDA via our security portal.

Implementation notes for engineers (short):
- Raw inputs/outputs: default hosted path stores ephemeral copies for 72h; persistent storage only if "long_trace" flag enabled on the tenant.
- Redaction: support for pre-send client-side redaction library + server-side PII scrubber. We recommend client-side hashing of sensitive fields (SHA-256) with customer-supplied salt (optional).
- Token logs: we can store token-level digests (SHA-256 of token sequences) for traceability; salts can be customer-provided and stored in your KMS via our KMS integration (we never store plaintext salts in hosted metadata).
- Audit trail: ingestion timestamps and purge events are recorded and can be exported as a signed JSON bundle for the period requested.

Attachments: I’ve re-attached the traceability PDF; it includes configurable knobs and sample API flags ("long_trace", "redact_policy": "client"/"server").

Can you confirm whether you want Option A (ephemeral-only) or Option B (30-day with PII redaction) for the pilot? If you need EU residency for the pilot we can schedule a dedicated EU tenant.

Thanks,
Hannah
[Attachment: redwood-prompt-traceability.pdf]
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: security notes for ClearHealth (answers + proposed pilot config)

Forwarding the security QA we drafted for ClearHealth so we’re aligned internally. Key engineering config we recommend for pilot: 

- Pilot config (recommended): Dedicated pilot tenant in US region + client-side hashing for direct identifiers + token-digest only logging (no plaintext token transcripts) + audit export enabled. Retention: ephemeral by default (0 days persistent) with an opt-in 30-day evaluation window controlled by the tenant admin.
- KMS: offer integration to allow ClearHealth to supply an AES key for salt storage; provide docs and an aspirational timeline for KMS onboarding (3–5 business days).
- Deliverables for pilot: (1) security answers PDF; (2) SOC 2 package under NDA; (3) technical onboarding doc showing API flags and sample redaction code.

I attached the security summary we can send to them (security-answers-CHS-20261102.pdf). If you both agree we should offer the dedicated pilot option (recommended for regulated PHI flows), I’ll scope out the Dedicated trial and estimate infra lead time.

Monica Patel
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: security-answers-CHS-20261102.pdf]

Subject: Next steps & mutual action plan for ClearHealth pilot

Sarah/Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Proposed MAP and timeline to keep momentum: 

1) Today–Nov 05: ClearHealth confirms pilot posture (Option A ephemeral-only OR Option B 30-day with client-side hashing).
2) Nov 06–Nov 10: Execute mutual NDA (we’ll send a standard one today) and request SOC 2 package delivery under NDA.
3) Nov 11–Nov 17: Technical onboarding — Dedicated pilot tenant provisioned in requested region; KMS integration if chosen.
4) Nov 18–Dec 02: 2-week pilot, with a security review checkpoint on Nov 25.

Deliverables from Redwood: proposed pilot config (JSON), security answers PDF, signed SOC2 docs under NDA, and a short onboarding playbook. Please confirm which option you want and whether you require EU residency for the pilot (we can provision an EU tenant). Once you confirm, I’ll create a HubSpot deal milestone and loop in our legal to push the NDA.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/67890

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
